text:
Luis Navarro: Heads-up: I'm prepping a promotion packet for Sofia. Two quick questions: 1) If we move someone from IC3 -> IC4, do we need director sign-off or is manager+skip-level enough? 2) Does changing band automatically change salary to midpoint).
Maya (People Ops): Quick answers: 1) IC3->IC4 usually needs director approval; IC4->IC5 requires director + VP sign-off. Check the checklist on the intranet for exceptions. 2) No, moves between bands do not auto-set salary to midpoint. Managers propose a comp number and we calibrate.
Priya Shah: Follow-up - what's required in the packet? I typically include impact bullets but want to make sure I'm not missing docs for calibration.
Maya (People Ops): Required items: manager justification (concise), 3-4 impact examples, peer/eng feedback (optional but helpful), proposed new title + base, current comp, any market data if available, and the approval chain. We prefer a single PDF or Google Doc with clear headers.
Devon Park: Is there a standard template for salary recommendation rationale? My managers vary widely in write-ups.
Maya (People Ops): Yes, we've got a 3-line template you can paste: 
```
Recommendation: Promote <Name> to <Title> effective <date>. Rationale: <one-sentence impact>. Proposed comp: $X base to $Y base (justification: market/peer parity/perf). Approvals: <names>."
```
Devon Park: Great - can you drop link?
Maya (People Ops): Link: https://intranet.redwood.com/people-ops/promo-templates (also pinned in the #people-ops channel).
Luis Navarro: Regarding effective date - if the manager wants it retroactive to the start of the month but submission happens after payroll cutoff, will payroll do retro pay?
Maya (People Ops): We can process retro pay up to the start of the fiscal month if there's documented approval BEFORE payroll run. If approval came after payroll close, it will be effective next pay period and backpay is possible with a payroll exception but only up to 60 days in practice. We try to avoid >1 month retro pay because of tax filing complexity.
Priya Shah: Does a title-only promotion (no comp change) need to go to calibration?
Maya (People Ops): If it's title-only and no band change, typically no calibration committee needed; manager and skip-level approval suffice. If title-only affects reporting or job family, ping People Ops so we can track org changes.
comp-ops-bot: FYI: Calibration meetings are held bi-weekly. Submission deadline for the next round: 1789990800 (UNIX ts). See: /calendar.
Devon Park: Can employees appeal a leveling decision? What's the timeframe and what evidence is useful?
Maya (People Ops): Appeals window = 10 business days from manager notification. Useful evidence: concrete examples of impact, product/customer outcomes, cross-team feedback, and any prior calibration artifacts. Start with manager conversation; if unresolved, submit appeals form and we'll route to an independent reviewer.
Luis Navarro: Equity - if we promote and grant a refresh, does that grant follow tenure vesting or restart?
Maya (People Ops): Refresh grants typically have their own vesting schedule (standard 4 yrs with 1 yr cliff unless stated). It does not alter existing grants. Details will be on the grant letter.
Priya Shah: Any guidance for communicating comp not approved at requested level? Managers sometimes struggle to explain.
Maya (People Ops): Use these points: 1) explain calibration rationale (market, internal parity), 2) highlight path to next band/comp (specific goals), 3) share timeline for re-review (6-12 months). We have canned manager language in the template library.
Devon Park: One more operational: who updates Workday after approval? Manager or People Ops?
Maya (People Ops): People Ops does the final system entry for promotions and comp changes to ensure data consistency. Managers must submit the packet and approvals; we update Workday and post the change.
Luis Navarro: Thanks, that's perfect. Will submit by end of day.
comp-ops-bot: Reminder: attach approval emails to the submission to avoid delays.
